sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the Cotton
Standardization Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Establishment of the institute

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
3. Establishment of the Institute.‑‑(1) There shall be
established an institute to be known as the Pakistan Cotton Standards Institute
which shall be a body corporate having perpetual succession and common seal and
may acquire, hold and dispose of its property:
Provided that the immovable
property of the Institute shall be disposed F after approval of the Federal
Government.
(2) The Head Office of the
Institute shall be at Karachi and the Board with the approval of the Federal
Government, set up offices at such other as and when required.
(3) The Institute may establish
such technical and administrative departments as it may consider necessary for
carrying out the purposes of this Ordinance.

Management

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
4. Management.‑‑(1) The general direction and
administration of the Institute shall vest in the Board which may exercise all
powers and do all acts which may be exercised or done by the Institute under
this Ordinance.
(2) ' The Board shall, in
discharge of its functions, act on sound principles of standardization, testing
and quality control, and shall be glided on matters of policy by such
directions as the Federal Government may give from time to time.
(3) If any question arises as
to whether any matter is a matter of policy or not, the decision of the Federal
Government shall be final.

Constitution of the board

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
5. Constitution of the Board.‑‑(1) The Board shall consist
of the following, namely:‑=
(i) The Chairman.
(ii) one representative each of
the Member
Ministry of Food, Agriculture and
Livestock, Ministry of Commerce
and Ministry of Finance,
Government of Pakistan.
(iii) one representative each
of the Members
Governments of the Punjab and
Sindh.
(iv) one representative each of
the Member
Cotton Export Corporation, Karachi
Cotton Association, All Pakistan
Textile Mills Association, Pakistan
Cotton Ginners Association and
Textile Commissioner's
Organization.
(v) one member each to be
appointed by Member
the Provincial Chambers of
Agriculture Punjab and Sindh to
represent cotton growers.
and
(vi) Director, Pakistan Cotton Standards Member/Secretary
Institute.
(2) The Chairman shall be
appointed by the Federal Government and hold office for a period of three years
and shall be eligible for re appointment.
(3) The Federal Government
shall, from amongst the members, appoint a member to be Vice‑Chairman of
the Board who shall hold office for a period of three years and shall be
eligible for reappointment.
(4) The appointment of the
Chairman, Vice‑Chairman and Members of the Board shall be notified in the
official Gazette.

Meeting

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
6. Meeting.‑‑‑(1) The meetings of the Board shall
be convened by the Chairman on such date and at such time and place as may be
specified by him:
Provided that no more than a
period of six months shall intervene between two meetings of the Board and at
least two meetings of the Board shall be held each year.
(2) On a written requisition of
at least three members, the Chairman shall, within a period of fifteen days
from receipt of such requisition, summon a meeting of the Board.
(3) Four members of the Board
shall constitute a quorum of a meeting of the Board.
(4) All decisions of the Board
shall be taken by majority vote and, in the event of equality of votes, the
Chairman shall have the casting vote.
(5) The Board may make rules
for conduct of its business.

Power of the board to associate other persons etc

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
7. Power of Board to associate other persons, etc.‑‑‑The
Board may, in such manner and on such terms as it may deem fit, seek the
advice or assistance of any person in carrying out the purposes of this
Ordinance and invite any person to take part in discussions during any of its
meeting without the right to vote.

Executive committee

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
8 Executive Committee. ‑‑‑(I) There shall be an
Executive Committee which shall consist of the following members, namely:‑‑‑
(a) the Chairman;
(b) three members of the Board
to be nominated by the Board; and
(c) Director, Pakistan Cotton
Standards Institute.
(2) Subject to the directions
of the Board, the Executive Committee shall be the principal administrative
body of the Institute and shall-----,
(a) be responsible for the
management and administration of all affairs of the Institute and control of
its funds within the overall policy and guidelines of the Board;
(b) undertake regular review
and evaluation of the performance of training, research, development and
implementation of projects and programmes of the Institute and submit a six‑monthly
report to the Board;
(c) scrutinize and submit the
annual development and non‑development budget of the Institute for
approval of the Board; and
(d) prepare draft rules of the
Board.

Appointment of officers and staff

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
9. Appointment of officers and staff .‑‑‑Subject to
such terms and conditions as may be laid down by the Federal Government, Board
may appoint such officers and staff as it considers necessary for the efficient
performance of the functions of the Institute.

Audit of accounts

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
10. Audit of Accounts.‑‑‑The annual accounts of the
Institute shall' be audited by the Auditor‑General of Pakistan or a
representative of the Federal Government specially appointed for this purpose.

Indemnification

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
11. Indemnification.‑‑‑Every officer and member of
staff, adviser and consultant of the Institute may be indemnified by the Board
against all losses and expenses sustained or incurred by him in good faith in
the discharge of the duties of his office.

Function of institute

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
12. Functions of the Institute. ‑‑‑The functions of
the Institute shall be to introduce and implement standardization and quality
control of cotton, and to‑‑‑
(a) establish cotton standards
and seed cotton grades for classification;
(b) prepare, approve, and
sanction standards boxes and seed cotton boxes;
(c) apply quality control for
export of cotton and its handling procedures in certified ginning factories;
(d) conduct classification of lint
cotton and to issue lint, cotton quality cards for each lot;
(e) conduct training of persons
in cotton grading and cotton classing of ginners, spinners and exporters of
public and private sectors institutions:
(f) settle disputes of
classification and grading amongst sellers and buyers of seed cotton and cotton
lint;
(g) apply cotton fibre testing
technologically using internationally accepted instrumentation, to review and
introduce improved methods of testing;
(h) recommend minimum premiums
and discounts for varying qualities of cotton;
(i) lay down the policy and
programme and its implementation for training in cotton classification,
arbitrations and appeals, and cotton fibre testing;
(j) issue post‑graduate
diplomas to successful trainees in cotton classification, arbitration and
appeals, and cotton fibre testing;
(k) provide for programme of
research, information and application of technology for cotton standardization;
and
(1) select technical officers
and other officers of the Institute.

Certified ginning factory

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
13. Certified Ginning Factory.‑‑‑(1) Every ginning .
factory having production in respect of five thousand bales per season shall be
deemed to be a certified ginning factory and shall follow the standardization
procedure and other technical requirements under this Ordinance and the rules
to be made thereunder.
(2) Two months before the
beginning of the ginning season, when it is satisfied the standardization
procedures and technical requirements shall be fulfilled by the ginning
factory, the Institute shall issue a standardization certificate to such
ginning factory under intimation to the concerned Provincial Government.

Cotton mixing and ginning of irregular cotton

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
14. Cotton Mixing and Ginning of Irregular Cotton. ‑‑‑Unless
otherwise directed by the Institute under this Ordinance‑‑---
(a) no ginner shall mix cotton
of different grades or staple lengths or irregular cotton with any graded
cotton; and
(b) any ginner who intends to
gin irregular cotton shall inform the Institute of his intention at least forty‑eight
hours before the ginning of irregular cotton.

Making of bales

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
15. Marking of Bales. ‑‑‑Notwithstanding
the marking requirements under Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966 (W.P. Ord. XX of
1966), any bale produced in a certified ginning factory shall be marked in such
manner as may he prescribed.

Placement of classes

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
16. Placement of Classers.‑‑‑(1) The Institute shall
assign a Classer to one 0 more certified ginning factories for supervision of
the standardization of cork,
(2) The assignment of Classer under
subsection (1) shall not prevent the Institute from exercising itself or any
Technical. Officer appointed by it from exercising the duties of a Classer.

Duties of classer

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
17. Duties of a Classer.‑‑‑(1)
The Classer shall supervise the implementation of standardization procedures
and technical requirements by the certified ginning factory or factories with
which his assignment has been made.
(2) In order to carry out his
duties under subsection (1), the Classer shall be empowered to visit the
assigned certified ginning factory and he may examine any cotton being ginned
and take samples thereof, except marked bales, for classification.
(3) If a Classer has reasons to
believe that the standardization procedures and technical requirements are not
complied with by a certified ginning factory, the Classer shall inform the
ginners by written memorandum with report to the Institute.

Quality control committee

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
18. Quality Control Committee.‑‑‑On receipt of the
report referred to in subsection (3) of section 17, the Institute may,
constitute a Quality Control Committee consisting of representative of the
ginners, Technical Officer and third party experts as may be prescribed and
direct the Committee in writing for verification of the report.

Duties of the quality control commission

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
19. Duties of the Quality
Control Committee. ‑‑‑The members of the Quality Control
Committee appointed under section 18 may visit the concerned certified ginning
factory and may examine any cotton and take samples thereof for verification.

Penalties

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
20. Penalties.‑‑‑(1)
Without prejudice to any penalty that may be imposed under any law for the time
being in force, any person who contravenes the provisions of section 14 shall
be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.
(2) Where a person is penalised
for any offence under this Ordinance or any rules made thereunder, the Court
may, in addition to such penalty, order for confiscation and sale of any mixed
cotton in respect of which the offence his been committed; '
Provided that 25 % of the sale
proceeds shall vest in the Fund;

Cognizance of offence

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
21. Cognizance of offence.‑‑‑No
Court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the first class shall try an offence
punishable under this Ordinance and no Court shall take cognizance of an
offence punishable under this Ordinance except upon a complaint made in writing
by the Institute or by a person authorised by the Board in this behalf.

sections.description:
Standardization fee

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
22. Standardization fee.‑‑‑The
Institute may charge standardization fee as charges of standardization of the
cotton at such rates as the Federal Government may, from time to time, fix by a
notification in the Official Gazette.

Pakistan cotton standard institute dun

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
23 Pakistan Cotton Standards
Institute Fund.‑‑‑(1) A fund, to be known as the
"Pakistan Cotton Standards Institute Fund" shall be established to
meet expenses in connection with the functions of the Institute under this
Ordinance including the payment of salaries and other remunerations of the
officers and staff of the Institute.
(2) The fund shall consist of‑‑‑
(a) grants made by the Federal
Government;
(b) loans obtained from the
Federal Government;
(c) loans obtained from, and
grants made by the foreign agencies with the prior sanction of the Federal
Government;
(d) fees charged under section
22; and
(e) all other funds, fines and
sums including donations received by the Institute;
(3) The Fund shall be kept in
the Personal Ledger Account of the Institute with the National Bank of Pakistan
or with such other banks as may be approved by the Federal Government.

Power of institute to borrow money

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
24. Power of the Institute to borrow money.‑‑‑For
borrowing money, the Institute shall be deemed to be a local authority
under the Local Authorities Loans Act, 1914 (IX of 1914).

Exemption from tax

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
25. Exemption from tax. ‑‑‑Notwithstanding
anything contained in the Income Tax Ordinance, 1979 (XXXI of 1979), all
contributions and donations to the Fund shall be exempt from the imposition of
income‑tax.

Budget

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
26. Budget.‑‑‑The
Institute shall prepare its annual budget estimates for every ensuing year, and
submit it for approval to the Federal Government.

Delegation

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
27. Delegation. ‑‑‑(I)
The Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, and
subject to such conditions as may be specified in the notification, direct that
all or any of its powers under this Ordinance or rules made thereunder shall be
exercisable by the Provincial Government or any authority subordinate to it.
(2) The Board may delegate all
or any of its powers under this Ordinance to the Chairman, member or any
officer of the Institute.

Power to make rules

ORDINANCE V OF 1997
ORDINANCE V OF 1997
COTTON STANDARDIZATION ORDINANCE, 1997
28. Power to make rules.‑‑‑(1)
The Board may, with the prior approval of the Federal Government and by a
notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes
of this Ordinance.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, these rules may provide
for all or any of the following matters, namely:‑‑
(a) standardization of cotton
and for application of standards;
(b) seed cotton grading and its
application;
(c) lint cotton classification
and its application;
(d) quality control of cotton
for export;
(e) selection and control of
certified ginning factories;
(f) fixing the allowed
variations between grades and staple lengths within the same lot;
(g) controlling the mixing of
grades, staple lengths, irregular cotton, salvaged cotton, delinted cotton, and
marking of bales according to their contents;
(h) empowering the Institute to
deliver written authorisation to a ginner to mix various grades of cotton;
(i) specification of technical
requirements which may be complied with by a certified ginning factory;
(j) regulating the composition
and the functions of technical and administrative departments, and other
offices of the Institute;
(k) levying of fees and charges
in respect of grading, classing, quality control, fibre testing and other
services provided by the Institute;
(1) settlement of disputes
between buyer and seller of cotton; and
(m) laying down the
qualifications and duties of Technical Officers and other officers of the
Institute.
